VERDICT: FAIL
BLOCKING: bench/coder/tasks/02-ring-buffer/tests.rs, `hidden_elements_dropped_exactly_once` - this test calls the solution's `new`, `push`, `pop_oldest`, `clear` and `drop` without `within(...)`, so a looping solution hangs this test until the whole cargo run is killed at `harness_timeout_seconds` (900 s) instead of failing after `test_timeout_seconds` (10 s). That breaks the brief's "Each test has a timeout" rule, and the README's claim that this test "cannot loop forever" is false.
MINOR: bench/coder/tasks/02-ring-buffer/tests.rs, `hidden_zero_capacity_panics` - it calls `RingBuffer::new(0)` directly without `within`, so the same unbounded-hang gap applies to this test.
MINOR: bench/coder/run.py, `provider_claude` - `subprocess.run(..., timeout=...)` raises an uncaught `TimeoutExpired`, which aborts the run before any result JSON is written; the already-paid model answers of earlier tasks survive only as raw files, and their costs never reach the result records.
MINOR: bench/coder/README.md, "Running a model" - the claim that no "project instructions or memory" reach the model is not checked for user-level memory (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`), which the headless CLI may still load; `check_workdir` only looks for project markers.
MINOR: bench/coder/harness.py, `grade_inner` - the model's code is compiled and run by `cargo test` on the local PC with no sandbox, so a solution can run arbitrary commands with the user's rights during grading; this is an accepted design cost, but it is not documented in the README's known limits.
